headline_marked: Own goal denies Egypt victory as [[Belgium escape with 1-1 draw]]
headline: Own goal denies Egypt victory as Belgium escape with 1-1 draw
summary: A late own goal forced Egypt to settle for a point in their opening 2026 World Cup match at Seattle Stadium.
details: Egypt faced Belgium in their opening Group G match of the 2026 World Cup at Seattle Stadium on Monday. The match ended in a 1-1 draw after a late equalizer from Belgium.

Midfielder Emam Ashour scored Egypt's only goal in the 19th minute with a superb 20-yard shot that beat Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois. It was Ashour's first international goal in his 30th appearance for the national team.

Egypt coach Hossam Hassan played Mohamed Salah centrally on the legend's 34th birthday. Salah provided a clinical pass to Ashour for the opening goal and nearly scored himself with a header in the 55th minute.
Belgium struggled in the first half, failing to test goalkeeper Mostafa Shoubir. However, they increased the pressure in the second half and introduced Romelu Lukaku in the 66th minute.

Just 28 seconds after entering the game, Lukaku forced an own goal as the ball deflected off Hany's foot in a crowded area in front of the goal. This equalizer prevented Egypt from securing their first-ever World Cup win.
Mohamed Salah was substituted off in the 75th minute. The match concluded with both teams sharing a point in their opening group stage fixture.

headline_marked: US Air Force [[B-52 bomber crashes in California]]
headline: US Air Force B-52 bomber crashes in California
summary: The long-range strategic bomber crashed shortly after takeoff from Edwards Air Force Base; casualties are yet to be confirmed.
details: A US Air Force B-52 Stratofortress bomber crashed in Southern California on Monday morning. The aircraft went down shortly after taking off from Edwards Air Force Base, according to base authorities.

The crash occurred at 11:20 AM local time, sending a massive plume of black smoke into the sky that was visible from several miles away. Emergency rescue teams arrived quickly at the scene and recovery operations are ongoing.
Authorities have not yet confirmed whether there were any casualties in the incident. Video footage from the air shows smoke still rising from the crash site.
The Boeing B-52, nicknamed 'The BUFF' (Big Ugly Fat Fellow), has been a staple of the US military since the 1950s. It is a long-range strategic bomber capable of flying at 50,000 feet.

The aircraft can carry approximately 70,000 pounds of weaponry, including hundreds of conventional bombs or 32 cruise missiles equipped with nuclear weapons. It can also be refueled mid-air, allowing it to strike anywhere in the world.

During the Cold War, the B-52 served as a 'nuclear umbrella' for the United States. Typically, the aircraft is operated by a crew of five, including a commander, pilot, radar navigator, navigator, and electronic warfare officer.
